verdicts.reason: The Electoral Commission oversight report says the LGERS register system is being migrated to Dublin City Council's tenancy on Microsoft Azure (US), a non-EU public cloud, so the hosting is non-EU.
The Revenue Commissioners (Ireland) say they run their own data centre and even host other public bodies from it, so this is state-operated national hosting.

An 'Oracle-based infrastructure platform' names Oracle's product, not who operates or hosts FMSS, and the implementation partner is neither named nor placed in a country, so no category is established.

The Central Bank of Ireland says T2 is a Eurosystem system governed by the ECB Guideline of 24 February 2022; the Eurosystem counts as EU, and the Bank's own data centre provider is not named, so nothing points to a non-EU host.

The Defence Forces CIS Corps (Ireland) runs the CISN as an on-premise national network built around two active/active data centres of its own; the cloud services it uses 'where required' are neither named nor tied to a country.

The 112/999 call-answering service is run under a State concession by BT, part of the UK's BT Group, and the NDRS/TETRA provider TETRA Ireland Communications is owned by Motorola Solutions (Chicago, US), so both parts are non-EU controlled.
